🔁 Oracle GoldenGate Replication Simulator

Change rows in the source database and watch Extract → Data Pump → Replicat copy them to the target in real time.

🟦 Source DB (ORCLSRC) · HR.EMP

🟩 Target DB (ORCLTGT) · HR.EMP

GGSCI (ogg-host) 1>
Try: INFO ALL · STOP REPLICAT REP1 (then change rows and see the lag grow) · START REPLICAT REP1 · STATS EXTRACT EXT1 · LAG REPLICAT REP1 · SEND EXTRACT EXT1, STATUS · HELP.
How it works: Extract reads committed changes from the source redo log and writes them to the local trail (./dirdat/lt). The Data Pump sends the trail across the network to the remote trail (./dirdat/rt). Replicat applies the changes to the target.

apps.title: Python Rock Paper Scissors
apps.about: Play against the computer and keep score.
apps.code:
# Rock, paper, scissors against the computer
import random

CHOICES = ["rock", "paper", "scissors"]
BEATS = {"rock": "scissors", "paper": "rock", "scissors": "paper"}
you = computer = 0

while True:
    mine = input("rock, paper or scissors? (q to quit): ").strip().lower()
    if mine == "q":
        break
    if mine not in CHOICES:
        print("Please type rock, paper or scissors.")
        continue
    theirs = random.choice(CHOICES)
    print("Computer chose", theirs)
    if mine == theirs:
        print("Draw 🤝")
    elif BEATS[mine] == theirs:
        print("You win! 🎉")
        you += 1
    else:
        print("Computer wins 🤖")
        computer += 1
    print(f"Score — you {you} : {computer} computer\n")

print(f"Final score — you {you} : {computer} computer")

apps.title: Python Password Generator
apps.about: Strong passwords using the secrets module.
apps.code:
# Strong password generator (uses the secrets module, made for passwords)
import secrets
import string

length = int(input("Password length (e.g. 16): ") or 16)
chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "!@#$%^&*()-_=+?"

# make sure it has at least one lowercase, uppercase, digit and symbol
while True:
    password = "".join(secrets.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))
    if (any(c.islower() for c in password) and any(c.isupper() for c in password)
            and any(c.isdigit() for c in password) and any(not c.isalnum() for c in password)):
        break

print("Your password:", password)

apps.title: Python Hangman
apps.about: Guess the word letter by letter.
apps.code:
# Hangman in the terminal
import random

WORDS = ["python", "computer", "elephant", "mango", "chennai", "rainbow"]
word = random.choice(WORDS)
guessed = set()
lives = 6

while lives > 0:
    shown = " ".join(c if c in guessed else "_" for c in word)
    print(f"\n{shown}   lives: {'♥' * lives}")
    if "_" not in shown:
        print("🎉 You got it!")
        break
    letter = input("Guess a letter: ").strip().lower()
    if len(letter) != 1 or not letter.isalpha():
        print("Type one letter.")
        continue
    if letter in guessed:
        print("You already tried that.")
        continue
    guessed.add(letter)
    if letter not in word:
        lives -= 1
        print("Nope!")
else:
    print(f"💀 Out of lives! The word was {word}.")

apps.title: Python Quiz
apps.about: Multiple-choice quiz with a final score.
apps.code:
# Quiz game: add your own questions to the list
QUESTIONS = [
    ("What is the capital of India?", ["Mumbai", "New Delhi", "Chennai", "Kolkata"], 2),
    ("How many planets are in the solar system?", ["7", "8", "9", "10"], 2),
    ("What is 12 x 12?", ["124", "144", "132", "156"], 2),
    ("Which gas do plants take in?", ["Oxygen", "Nitrogen", "Carbon dioxide", "Hydrogen"], 3),
]

score = 0
for number, (question, options, answer) in enumerate(QUESTIONS, 1):
    print(f"\nQ{number}. {question}")
    for i, option in enumerate(options, 1):
        print(f"  {i}) {option}")
    choice = input("Your answer (1-4): ").strip()
    if choice == str(answer):
        print("✅ Correct!")
        score += 1
    else:
        print(f"❌ The answer was {options[answer - 1]}")

print(f"\nYou scored {score} out of {len(QUESTIONS)} ({score * 100 // len(QUESTIONS)}%)")
